name: Algolaser Alpha MK2 20W
tagline: 20W Premium open-frame diode focused on speed and fine engraving detail
tldr: Algolaser Alpha MK2 20W is the 20W SKU on the Algolaser algolaser alpha mk2 line. Algolaser targets makers who want faster engraving and tighter spot control than typical budget diodes. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

priceRange.note: 20W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Algolaser's settings cut 8 mm basswood plywood at 200 mm/min and 12 mm at 100 mm/min, each in one pass
Black acrylic up to 8 mm in one pass (100 mm/min)
Most affordable Alpha MK2: $579 machine-only, $729 in the basic kit (October 2026)
cons: Spot widens to 0.16 × 0.14 mm at full power (0.06 × 0.05 mm at 3%): cutting and fine engraving need different focus habits
13–15 mm plywood drops to 2 passes, where the 40W stays at one: compare both if thick stock is planned
Open frame: fumes and eye safety are on you unless you add Algolaser's smart enclosure ($929 bundle)
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Algolaser Alpha MK2. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.

editorialDepth.advantages: Algolaser Alpha MK2 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU: clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame: glasses and exhaust required. Upgrade path to 40W if cutting takes over. Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.

faq.question: How thick can the Alpha MK2 20W cut in one pass?
faq.answer: Algolaser's material settings list basswood plywood at 700 mm/min (3 mm), 300 mm/min (5–6 mm), 200 mm/min (8 mm) and 100 mm/min (10–12 mm), all in one pass at 100% power; 13–15 mm take 2 passes. Black acrylic: 5–8 mm in one pass at 100 mm/min, 10 mm in 2 passes.

faq.question: How much does the Alpha MK2 20W cost compared with the 40W?
faq.answer: On Algolaser's store in October 2026: $579 machine-only, $729 basic kit, $809 pro kit and $919 safe kit for the 20W, against $999 machine-only and $1,149 basic kit for the 40W. That is about a $420 gap at the machine-only level. The 20W smart enclosed bundle was $929.

faq.question: 20W or 40W: which suits a side business?
faq.answer: The 20W covers most side businesses that cut up to 8–12 mm plywood and engrave every day. The 40W earns its extra $420 mainly on throughput: 3 mm plywood at 750 vs 700 mm/min is close, but 8 mm runs at 350 vs 200 mm/min and 15 mm stays single-pass. Pick the 40W if long cutting jobs fill your week.

standoutFeatures.title: 12 mm plywood in one pass
standoutFeatures.body: Algolaser's own settings cut 10–12 mm basswood plywood in a single pass at 100 mm/min with the 20W module.

standoutFeatures.title: Fine at low power
standoutFeatures.body: Algolaser specifies a 0.06 × 0.05 mm spot at 3% power, which keeps light photo engraving detailed while full power handles cutting.

standoutFeatures.title: Balanced price
standoutFeatures.body: $579 machine-only in October 2026, about $420 less than the 40W for the same software and accessories ecosystem.
